laws.rule: Northern Territory government says designated campsites in its parks and reserves must be booked and paid online before camping; payment is not taken at the park. A separate permit is required to camp outside marked camping grounds or to enter and camp overnight at Garig Gunak Barlu National Park / Cobourg Peninsula.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: Pets are generally not permitted in Northern Territory parks and reserves, but the government lists specified places and conditions where dogs are allowed. Check the park and its signs; permitted hunting dogs are subject to separate rules.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: For Northern Territory parks and reserves, recreational drone use is park-specific: some parks prohibit it and some require an aircraft-operation permit. A trade and commerce permit is required for commercial drone flights. Check the Territory list; Kakadu and Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa have separate Parks Australia rules.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: When drone flight is permitted in Northern Territory parks, government rules include staying at least 200 m from or not flying over occupied waterholes, campgrounds and picnic areas, staff houses, offices and workshops, and obtaining people's consent to photograph or record them. Follow CASA rules and any park-specific restrictions.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: NT parks booking conditions say fires may be lit only in designated fireplaces or as park signs allow, and generators only where authorised or signed as permitted. Obey any fire ban and check current conditions.
